data.name: Pawanraj
data.gender_notes: Pawanraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who governs the wind and rain, the king of nature. The name Pawanraj carries the meaning “Lord of the Wind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Pawanraj usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the wind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of nature and the divine will
data.etymology: Pawanraj belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Wind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pawanraj total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pawanraj holds a deep cultural significance as it stems from the Hindu religious tradition, where the god Vayu (Hindu God of Wind) or Pawan is revered and often depicted as a king or ruler of the sky and elements. The name Pawanraj suggests this divine connection and acknowledges the power and influence of the natural world.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Pawanraj lies in the veneration of the divine presence of Vayu as a ruler or king. It serves as a constant reminder of our connection to the natural world and the basic elements that sustain life. The spiritual name also inspires one to live in harmony with nature, understanding the cycles of wind and rain as a part of the larger cosmic order.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Pawanraj: Lord of the Winds. Embodiment of change and motion, symbolizing freedom and progress. Carrier of new ideas and experiences.

historical_references.reference: Pawanraj was a Jain monk and scholar during the 12th-13th century in India. He is known for his contributions to Jain literature, particularly in the fields of grammar, rhetoric, and logic.
historical_references.context: The Jain tradition is one of the oldest Indian religions, characterized by its emphasis on nonviolence, asceticism, and spiritual purification. Pawanraj lived and contributed to this intellectual tradition during a period of flourishing Jain scholarship in medieval India.

historical_references.reference: Pawanraj is also known for his role as a royal advisor to King Vaghela of Gujarat in the 13th century. He used his knowledge of logic and rhetoric to help the king navigate political conflicts and make informed decisions.
historical_references.context: The Vaghela dynasty ruled the Gujarat region from the late 10th to the early 15th century. Pawanraj's expertise in logic and rhetoric made him a valuable advisor to the king, particularly during periods of political instability and conflict.
